background: ABN AMRO is a Dutch retail, private and commercial bank, part-owned by the Dutch state since its rescue, funded largely by domestic deposits and lending mainly on Dutch residential mortgages and to Northwest European businesses.
synthesis: The rating picture is solid: A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, one on a positive outlook and two on a stable outlook, and the last move was a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is the softer side against EU and Nordic peers, with CET1 of 15.3% below the peer median and leverage of 4.8% under the peer median, though CET1 has risen 1.5 points since 30 Jun 2024. Liquidity is the strength: LCR of 157% is above the peer median and NSFR of 141% sits in the top quarter. The flagged news is mostly earnings beats, the newest on 12 Aug 2026, with an older anti-money-laundering shortcomings item worth noting.
